title: On-call Context Bundles and Shift Handoff Cookbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This cookbook defines a lightweight, repeatable format for packaging and transferring operational context between platform operators during shift handoffs, incident rotations, and cross-team escalation. It is targeted at platform operators and SREs running Redwood inference services (hosted, dedicated, and private) and emphasizes:

- Minimum viable context to avoid cognitive load.
- Machine-friendly bundles that can be attached to alerts and runbooks.
- Clear ownership and next-step actions to reduce time-to-stable.

Why this exists

Handoffs are frequent in a global service like Redwood. We observed the following pain points in retrospectives:
1) Incoming operator lacks quick access to the last relevant remediation attempts and why they failed.
2) Important telemetry (prefix cache rates, token burst patterns) is not surfaced in a single place.
3) Context transfer is often free-form text in PagerDuty comments which is hard to query or reuse.

Goals

- Define a one-page human summary + compact machine-readable bundle.
- Provide templates and CLI examples to generate the bundle from tooling.
- Integrate bundles into alert pages and incident channels.

Scope and audience

- Applies to platform services (router, batcher, kv-prefix-cache, model-proxy, scheduler) and operator teams listed in our ownership matrix.
- Not intended to replace full incident writeups; it is a short-lived operational artifact that travels with an alert and is persisted to the incident only if the oncall decides.

Bundle format (human + machine)

We recommend a two-part artifact attached to every major alert or handoff: 1) Handoff Summary (human-readable, ~200–400 words) and 2) Context Bundle (JSON payload, <= 12KB). The JSON is stored in the alert's metadata and can be rendered by dashboards. Example fields:

Handoff Summary (example)

- Time window: 2026-09-12T02:02Z — 2026-09-12T02:35Z
- Service impacted: prefix-cache-service (region: us-west-2)
- Symptom: sudden drop in prefix_cache_hit_rate for high-qps tenants; correlated token surge from tenant-42 after rollout v2.1.3
- Actions attempted: rolled back canary model-variant -> model-variant-stable, increased batcher soft limit to 128 tokens, triggered cache rehydrate job (id: rh-20260912-001).
- Current status: degraded, partial mitigation in progress, elevated SLO burn (error budget remaining: 41%).
- Recommended next steps: maintain rollback, monitor rehydrate job for 5 minutes, schedule follow-up with customer-success if tenant-42 still shows anomalies.

Context Bundle (fields to include in JSON)

- alert_id (string)
- time_range (ISO8601 start/end)
- service (one of: router,batcher,kv-prefix-cache,model-proxy,scheduler)
- region
- important_metrics: list of metric=>last_value pairs (token_rate, prefix_cache_hit_rate, avg_latency_95p, eviction_rate)
- recent_actions: list of short actions with timestamp and actor (e.g., rollback, scale-up, config-toggle)
- relevant_runs: runbook_job_ids, deck links, or synthetic test IDs
- owner_oncall
- escalation_contacts
- last_similar_incident_id (if applicable)

Note: the JSON should avoid including sensitive logs or customer PII. If required, store sensitive traces in the secure evidence store and reference by ID.

Minimum Handoff Checklist (for human ops)

1. One-line summary (symptom + region + service).
2. Current impact & SLO burn (exact numbers).
3. Top 3 metrics to watch with alert thresholds.
4. Last 3 remediation steps (what, who, when).
5. Recommended next step and who should be paged.
6. Links: dashboard, runbook, incident channel, rollback artifact.

Operator-produced artifacts (templates)

A. Handoff Summary template (paste into incident channel):

[Handoff Summary]
Time window: {{start}} — {{end}}
Service: {{service}} (region: {{region}})
Impact: {{brief impact sentence}}
Top metrics: {{metric1}}={{value1}}, {{metric2}}={{value2}} ...
Actions attempted: 1) {{action1}} 2) {{action2}}
Status: {{open|in_progress|resolved}}
Next step: {{next_step}} (@{{who}})
Link: {{dashboard_link}} | Runbook: {{runbook_link}}

B. Context Bundle JSON schema (human-readable spec)

| field | type | example | notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| alert_id | string | pgrd-20260912-07 | unique alert key |
| time_range | string | 2026-09-12T02:02Z/2026-09-12T02:35Z | ISO8601 interval |
| service | string | kv-prefix-cache | one of our services |
| region | string | eu-west-1 | |
| important_metrics | list | [{"token_rate": 12000}, {"prefix_cache_hit_rate": 0.26}] | include 3–6 metrics |
| recent_actions | list | ["rollback:model-variant-stable@02:10Z","scale:batcher+32@02:14Z"] | chronological |
| owner_oncall | string | @june-wang | person who last acted |
| escalation_contacts | list | ["oncall-pagerduty:platform","se-cust:security"] | roles or channels |

Automating bundle creation

We provide two helpers in the platform operator CLI (platformctl) and a lightweight lambda (hook) that can attach the bundle to the PagerDuty event when triggered by an alert rule.

platformctl example:

# generate a bundle and print as compressed base64 (safe for alert payloads)
platformctl handoff create --alert-id pgrd-20260912-07 --service kv-prefix-cache --region us-west-2 --metrics token_rate:12000,prefix_cache_hit_rate:0.26,avg_latency_95p:420 --action "rollback:model-variant-stable@02:10Z" --owner @june-wang | jq -C .

Lambda hook pseudo-YAML (used by alerting infra):

trigger: pagerduty.webhook
actions:
  - run: platformctl handoff create --from-webhook $WEBHOOK_PAYLOAD --compress | attach_to_alert $ALERT_ID

Runbook cross-links

Each service runbook must include a "Handoff bundle consumption" section describing: how to unpack the bundle, where to find referenced evidence, and what automated checks to run on intake. Example quick checks:

- Verify time_range in bundle matches alert window.
- Run quick health checks: curl /health, query prefix_cache_hit_rate via metrics API, run a synthetic request to the model-proxy.
- Check last remediation actions and validate rollback state (model variant, feature-flag).

Quick diagnostics checklist (for shift handoff)

1) Authenticate to region console (us-west-2 / eu-west-1).
2) Open dashboard link from bundle; validate metric spikes against short tail synthetic test.
3) Check prefix cache hit-rate and evictions: threshold for urgent escalation: hit_rate < 0.35 and eviction_rate > 0.02 (5-min rolling).
4) Confirm batcher queue depth and average request size.
5) If token_rate > 10k/min and avg_latency_95p > 400ms, reduce routing to canary model variant or increase batcher capacity.

SLO and operational thresholds to display in handoff

- prefix_cache_hit_rate (5m rolling): target >= 0.7; urgent if < 0.35
- avg_latency_95p (ms): target < 250; urgent if > 400
- token_rate (per-region, per-tenant 5m): expected baseline + 3x burst tolerance; alert if > baseline * 4
- eviction_rate (5m): target < 0.01; urgent if > 0.02

Escalation matrix (short)

- Tier 1 (operator oncall): investigate, try recommended runbook steps, attach updated bundle.
- Tier 2 (platform duty): if urgent thresholds hit or mitigation absent after 10 minutes.
- Tier 3 (oncall lead + service owner): for cross-region or multi-tenant impact, or when incident exceeds 30 minutes.

Handoff etiquette and communication guidelines

- Keep the summary concise: treat the handoff message like a tweet + reference pack.
- Always attach the Context Bundle to the alert and incident channel.
- If you inherit an ongoing remediation, explicitly state what you will not change.
- Use explicit sign-offs: ACTIONS_DONE: [action1,action2] NEXT_ONCALL: @name

Training and adoption roadmap

1. Q3 2026: Pilot with 3 platform SREs for the router and kv-prefix-cache services.
2. Q4 2026: Integrate bundle creation into 50% of alert rules for critical services.
3. Q1 2027: Full rollout and include bundle metrics in operator onboarding curriculum.

Retrospective template (for handoffs that led to incidents)

- What was transferred correctly? (list)
- What was missing and caused rework? (list)
- Time-cost of context retrieval (minutes)
- Actions to prevent recurrence (owner + target date)

Appendix A — Example incident handoff (realistic, redacted)

Handoff Summary: 2026-06-18T11:20Z — 11:45Z | service: model-proxy (eu-west-1) | Symptom: elevated 95p latency during rolling kernel update. Actions: paused rolling, reverted kernel to 6.1.14, rehydrated kv-prefix-cache rh-20260618-04. Status: stable. Next: schedule canary on 3 hosts, track 24h.

Context Bundle (base64 snippet): eyJhbGVydF9pZCI6ICJwZ3JkLTIwMjYwNjE4LTA0IiwgIm1ldHJpY3MiOiB7InRva2VuX3JhdGUiOiAxNTI3fX0=

Appendix B — Useful CLI snippets

# Unpack and pretty print bundle attached to an alert (platformctl + jq)
platformctl handoff get --alert-id pgrd-20260912-07 | base64 --decode | jq .

# Quick metric snapshot for handoff (returns only the canonical metrics)
platformctl metrics snapshot --service kv-prefix-cache --region us-west-2 --metrics token_rate,prefix_cache_hit_rate,avg_latency_95p --window 5m

Ownership & maintenance

- Primary owner: Platform Observability (eng-platform)
- Secondary owner: Oncall tooling (eng-sre)
- Review cadence: Bundle schema and runbook links reviewed quarterly (next review: 2027-01-15)

Related pages

- Platform operator handbook (runbook) — /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/platform-operator-handbook-degraded-kv-prefix-cache-2026
- Oncall training curriculum — /confluence/eng-platform/team-wiki/operator-onboarding-certification-pathway-2026

Feedback and improvements

Email the owners or open a PR against the handoff-bundle schema repository. When in doubt, prefer adding a short bundle field rather than freeform notes.
